territorial_scope.description: Applies to elections in Arizona, as the act amends the Arizona Revised Statutes and covers candidates on the ballot in an election.

evidence.quote: Title 16, chapter 7, article 1, Arizona Revised Statutes, is amended by adding section 16-1023

summary.short: Adds Arizona Revised Statutes section 16-1023. Within ninety days before an election with a candidate on the ballot, creators may not distribute a deceptive, fraudulent deepfake of that candidate unless it carries a clear and conspicuous AI-generated disclosure. Satire, parody and interactive computer services are excluded.
summary.long: SB 1359 adds section 16-1023 to Title 16, chapter 7, article 1 of the Arizona Revised Statutes, concerning election communications. Within ninety days before an election at which a candidate for elected office will appear on the ballot, a person who acts as a creator may not create and distribute a synthetic media message that the person knows is a deceptive and fraudulent deepfake of that candidate on that ballot, unless the message includes a clear and conspicuous disclosure that it includes content generated by artificial intelligence. A creator is a person who uses artificial intelligence or other digital technology to generate synthetic media, and the term excludes providers of the technology used. The prohibition does not apply to media that constitutes satire or parody, or to an interactive computer service as defined in 47 United States Code section 230. A person who fails to make the required disclosure is liable for the civil penalty prescribed by section 16-937, subsection B, for each day the deceptive and fraudulent deepfake is distributed without disclosure. The act defines a deceptive and fraudulent deepfake as synthetic media that depicts a candidate with knowledge of its falsity and intent to injure the candidate's reputation, and that is intentionally calculated to mislead a reasonable person. It contains a severability clause. The text states no effective date.

notes: Section 16-937 is not reproduced in this text; its location in Title 16 is inferred from the amendment context. The text gives no effective date, session law number or enactment history. Subsection A prohibits deceptive deepfakes only within ninety days before an election, and subsection D(2) requires knowledge of falsity and intent to injure reputation; subsection D(1)(b) excludes technology providers from the term creator. Section 2 is a severability clause.
